_about: Data for tools/readme_images.py: the README's benchmark poster (docs/assets/benchmarks-*.webp) and header (docs/assets/header-*.svg).
A cell is {"value": tok/s, "method": speculative decoding method}, null (renders as a dash: not measured or not supported) or "x" (renders as ×: can't run that model on a Mac).
An engine whose numbers all share one method shows it under its name; otherwise each number shows its own. "todo" and "note" are never rendered; the script prints the todos.

Numbers: decode tok/s at T = 0.6 (docs/benchmarks.md, The README's tables; Flint at its card's T = 1.0, each of its cells the mean of that engine's 2026-10-22 runs, prefill and decode from the same runs; the M5 Pro's Kapitsa cell is the mean of the two on runs of #345's serve ABBA (NI_FLINT_QATTN on, 631bd25, one run per pass, prefill and decode from the same runs; the forward run is flagged for contention, and both for prompt sizes checked against the default corpus's references); the M1 Pro's 2-bit row: runs alternated with llama.cpp, Kapitsa's prefill from an earlier swap-free run, and llama.cpp's cell its one decode phase without swap (greedy), with no prefill), Kapitsa's KFlash runs on the M4 Pro as noted; "prefill" on a cell is the 4K-prompt reading speed from bench/results. Kapitsa's prefill is from its newest run without a contention or invalid flag (the M5 Pro's Flint cell, above, is one exception: two runs that carry the invalid flag, one of them the contention flag too; the M5 Max's Kapitsa and Splash cells are another: 2026-10-22 runs on main, each flagged for contention, Bolt's decode median including two repetition-loop runs), and its decode is the number in the cell's decode column; they can come from different runs (the M5 Pro's 27B Kapitsa cell is the median of three flag-free Kapitsa-only runs on 2026-10-23 on main b7580af (#360), after a discarded first launch, prefill and decode each that column's median, and its mlx-serve cell the mean of that engine's two 2026-10-22 runs on main 16f2b6a, prefill and decode from those runs; the M5 Pro's 35B-A3B cell is the median of three flag-free Kapitsa-only runs on 2026-10-23 on main 920542c (#365), after a discarded first launch, prefill and decode each that column's median, and its Lightning cell is a single 2026-10-21 run with prefill and decode together). The other engines' prefill is from the stored run closest to the decode value shown, flagged or not; the M5 Pro's Splash cells are each the mean of two 2026-10-22 runs between two Kapitsa runs (ABBA), every one flagged for contention, prefill and decode from those runs, except the 35B-A3B's decode, which is the loop-free run alone (the other run has a repetition-loop answer).

tables._about: The README's Models section: one collapsed dropdown per Mac (python3 readme_images.py --tables). A Mac's rows are its poster rows, then its rows here; a Mac not on the poster has only these. "models" names each row's model in the tables, keyed by the rows' "model". A cell's "detail" shows under its method in the tables only; a Mac's "caption" shows under its table. "families" splits each Mac's dropdown into one table per family, in this order (a Mac with one family has one table); an engine gets a column in a family's table only where it has a number there; "versions" replaces an engine's poster version in the tables' headers.

macs.title: MacBook Pro (16-inch, 2023) · M3 Pro · 36 GB
macs.caption: macOS 14.1, on AC power: Kapitsa's macOS 14 kernels (macOS 15 and later run fused ones). mlx-serve, oMLX and Splash need a newer macOS (×); LM Studio was not installed; rec 0.1.0 refuses this Mac: it requires 48 GiB. Each cell but Flint's is one run of the M4 Pro's protocol (Flint's is the mean of two runs, #341), the other engines in the M4 Pro's setup (not re-tuned here). Nano 4B and 9B v2: Kapitsa runs NVIDIA's published checkpoints, which keep some layers in BF16/FP8, so it reads more per token than the 4-bit files: the 4B's FP8 is ~1 byte per weight against Q4_K_M's ~0.6, the 9B's NVFP4 ~6.11 GB per token against 4.67 GB for mlx-lm's 4-bit. Nano 9B v2 on mlx-lm: no prefill shown, because its template ignores enable_thinking and the timed first token is a thinking token.
